deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is not a mathematical manuscript but lecture notes on ancient history, written in German Kurrent script. It continues the previous page on the Neo-Babylonian empire and begins a section 'IV. Phönizier'. The arrangement resembles a Heeren-style survey of ancient states and trade, which is my inference. The hand and content suggest a student's notebook bound into or catalogued with the bundle, not a Gauss working sheet.

Content in order:
(1) Babylon ends with Cyrus in 538 BC. The Babylonians are described as a highly cultivated people, versed in astronomy and the art of measuring ('Meßkunst'), living in great splendour and luxury. Babylon was a seat of manufactures, especially weaving and dyeing.
(2) 'Landhandel' (overland trade): there were close ties with Phoenicia through a caravan route via Palmyra. Wine came from Armenia, and there were close links with Persepolis and Susa. Eastward trade reached northern India (Tibet), the source of gemstones and dyestuffs, especially cochineal.
(3) 'Seehandel' (sea trade): this ran over the Persian Gulf to India and (eastern?) Africa.
(4) 'IV. Phönizier': the Phoenicians were not a conquering people, yet they spread more widely than the earlier peoples. Their inventions include alphabetic writing (attributed to Taaut/Thoth), glass and purple dyeing. Through seafaring they tied other peoples together.

There are no formulas, computations or derivations to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors. A historical point: attributing cochineal to Babylonian trade with India/Tibet is an anachronism. Cochineal is a New World dyestuff, although 18th/19th-century authors sometimes used the term loosely for kermes-type red dyes. This slip belongs to the lecture notes, not the transcription.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Sie waren nur als' should likely read 'Sie werden uns als ein äusserst cultivirtes Volk geschildert'.
'Laut erfand die Buchstabenschrift' should likely read 'Taaut erfand die Buchstabenschrift'. Taaut/Thoth is the legendary inventor of letters in the Sanchuniathon tradition.
'Diese waren kein erobernd Volk haben sie aber' should likely read 'Diese waren kein eroberndes Volk, haben sich aber doch viel mehr verbreitet'.
'Färbereien besonders Cochenille' (in the trade passage) is probably 'Farbwaaren/Färbewaaren, besonders Cochenille'.
'dem westlichen[?] Afrika' is possibly 'dem östlichen Afrika'. The reading is uncertain.
'Sie schlugen durch die Schifffahrt' reads in the image like 'Sie schlungen durch die Schiffahrt ein allgemeines Band um andere Völkern', i.e. 'schlangen' (wound a bond around other peoples).
Page number '11' is at the top right; the heading begins 'Cyrus 538.'
